timing_disclosure.integrity_disclosure_is_separate: The parent-reported exposure is not erased by this reviewer remaining blind; this note neither certifies nor repairs study blinding.

frozen_design.scope: Known four tasks, seed 57, four timing-by-representation arms, sixteen planned cells, at most two checkpoint opportunities in every arm. Seed/task development scope selected using prior activation evidence. Old cohorts and controls are not pooled.
frozen_design.treatment_precision: Initial focus packet is shared. Delta is eligible only at the second opportunity when the first summary was accepted; opportunity two need not be dispatched or accepted. Accepted delta preserves the prior note bytes and adds a new note. No third opportunity exists.
frozen_design.exposure_rule: E sums positive parts of observed native actor-input token differences when deleting only newly eligible raw history from otherwise identical count-only views. Only already dispatched, known terminal actor calls contribute. C is the latest known paid focus logical input plus output. Repeated exposure timing offers at E >= C, with shared freshness/retention/opportunity limits. Neither current unsent input nor predicted future savings is added.
frozen_design.acceptance_and_cost: The complete proposed actor view must be natively shorter and satisfy combined size/context/budget constraints. Byte retention does not verify summary truth. Every role logical input plus output is counted; cached input is not deducted. Unknown and missing costs remain distinct from zero.

search_scope.selection: Two directly relevant papers and the official incremental-summary implementation document. TurnCost was reused only through the prior local review, not reverified here; Hermes was selected instead to inspect the immutable-note versus rewritten-running-summary distinction.
search_scope.scope_limit: Targeted method-section comparison, not a systematic novelty search or priority review. No search absence is evidence of novelty.

verified_primary_sources.title: StateComp: Learning When to Compress History in Long Horizon Agents
verified_primary_sources.evidence: READY scores and span gates determine execution. A summary must be valid and shorter under the same serialization/tokenizer; this does not imply semantic fidelity. Appendix E.4 subtracts summary input/output cost from cumulative subsequent input reductions on a fixed sequence and warns that online behavior may change.
verified_primary_sources.overlap: Cost-inclusive compression, shorter-view validation and cumulative savings accounting are established.
verified_primary_sources.difference_in_viewed_method: P139 uses past counterfactual deletion-view exposure versus the previous focus charge to offer a future second compaction. That differs from the READY gate and from accounting for realized later savings after a replacement.
verified_primary_sources.inference_limit: The accounting identity does not establish payback or competitiveness of the P139 trigger; no exact-match absence outside the inspected sections is asserted.

verified_primary_sources.title: Self-Compacting Language Model Agents
viewed_scope: Section 3 summarizer/trigger/compaction loop and cost analysis
verified_primary_sources.evidence: A periodic same-model rubric chooses whether to summarize. Summarization instructions are appended to reuse context, and the resulting summary replaces the prior trajectory. The comparison includes fixed-interval compaction, additional calls and cache-aware cost accounting.
verified_primary_sources.overlap: Adaptive compaction, fixed-interval controls and counting summarizer overhead are not new.
verified_primary_sources.difference_in_viewed_method: P139 uses a deterministic measured E/C trigger rather than a semantic rubric. Its eligible second delta keeps the old note bytes. Appending an instruction for cache reuse is not the same representation as preserving an old summary and adding a delta.
verified_primary_sources.inference_limit: Logical token reduction is distinct from monetary savings. These differences do not establish that immutable delta memory is new.

verified_primary_sources.title: Hermes Agent micro-compaction
verified_primary_sources.version: Mutable main documentation; commit and historical priority not verified
verified_primary_sources.evidence: The documented loop summarizes an old unsummarized exchange together with the running summary, replacing the latter with an updated summary. A threshold triggers later defragmentation. The document describes cadence controls and warns that history rewriting can harm cache reuse.
verified_primary_sources.overlap: Incremental summary maintenance and cost-conscious compaction cadence already exist.
verified_primary_sources.difference_in_viewed_method: The documented running summary is rewritten; P139 preserves the first note bytes and adds a delta only at its eligible second opportunity.
verified_primary_sources.inference_limit: This is a narrow comparison with the documented algorithm, not a whole-repository or historical-priority audit. Incremental or append-only memory in general is not claimed new.

claim_limits.current_conclusion: There are narrow, testable control and representation differences, amid substantial known compaction and incremental-memory overlap. The bounded source review does not establish technical novelty. Frozen controls can support a scoped empirical comparison after closure; they cannot substitute for a novelty argument or statistical interaction analysis.
safe_mechanism_statements: The frozen E/C trigger is a concrete retrospective exposure heuristic that can be compared with the frozen threshold control. E is a positive-part count difference, not a claim of recoverable future savings; C does not bound the next summary cost.

The second-opportunity delta policy tests retaining one previous summary verbatim while summarizing new raw history. It changes representation under common acceptance limits, without proving fidelity, freshness or conflict resolution.

Limiting every arm to two opportunities removes a possible third-trigger feedback from changed delta summary cost. It does not align threshold and exposure timing, force activation, or ensure every representation pair has a matched observed prefix.
claim_limits.gate_is_not_statistical_interaction: Passing the fixed primary/both-control dominance gates, or success of all four arms, is not a statistical timing-by-representation interaction, synergy, broad noninferiority, novelty, or independent replication.
claim_limits.gate_vs_interaction_reason: Dominance tests inequalities against controls. An interaction concerns whether a representation contrast changes with timing; those are different propositions.
claim_limits.development_scope_limit: Four known development tasks at one selected seed do not establish a population interaction, a noninferiority margin/test, or an independent confirmatory replication. A zero observed loss is not a general quality guarantee.
claim_limits.observed_prefix_limit: Recorded prefix matching constrains observed differences before treatment. It does not certify all hidden runtime state or semantic equivalence; opaque output identifiers can also cause strict hash mismatch. A missing or mismatched proof must remain a limitation, not be repaired by assuming equivalence.
unproven_claims: First adaptive, cost-triggered, amortized or incremental compaction method.
A novel immutable/delta-memory mechanism merely because the three viewed methods differ.
Ski-rental competitiveness, guaranteed payback, future savings or semantic preservation.
Statistical synergy, broad noninferiority, general task success, held-out generalization or independent replication.
Novelty from strong controls, source binding, matched-prefix checks or complete accounting alone.
